title: Slow-cooker pork and bean stew
subtitle: Pork shoulder braised with butter beans and paprika
excerpt: Pork shoulder cooked low and slow with butter beans, tinned tomatoes, and smoked paprika. A rich, warming stew that improves with every hour.
sourceNotes: Pork and bean stews are a staple of Spanish and Portuguese home cooking, where the combination appears in dishes like fabada asturiana and feijoada. This version uses butter beans and smoked paprika in the Spanish style.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the hob.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The flavour improves overnight. Make the day before and reheat gently.

content.text: Pork shoulder is the best cut for this recipe. It has enough fat to stay moist over a long cook and the connective tissue breaks down into the sauce as it cooks. The butter beans become very creamy and help thicken the broth. After 7 to 8 hours, both the pork and the beans will have absorbed the smoked paprika deeply.
No browning is needed here. The pork can go in raw and the slow cook develops all the flavour. If you do have time to brown the pork first, the finished stew will be slightly richer.
Serve with crusty bread or rice. A sharp green salad alongside cuts through the richness.

Place {{pork-shoulder}} of pork shoulder chunks in the slow cooker. Add {{butter-beans}} of drained butter beans, {{onion}} sliced onion, and {{garlic}} of crushed garlic. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes, {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree, and {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock. Add {{smoked-paprika}} of smoked paprika, {{thyme}} of thyme, and {{bay-leaves}} of bay. Season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt.
Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 7 to 8 hours. The pork should be very tender and beginning to break apart. Discard the bay and thyme. Taste and adjust the seasoning before serving.

rows.symptom: The pork is still tough after 8 hours
rows.cause: Pork shoulder with more bone than expected, or a very large piece, may take longer.
rows.fix: Switch to HIGH for a further hour. The collagen in the shoulder takes time to break down; once it does, the pork will become very tender quickly.

rows.cause: The pork and beans released more liquid than expected.
rows.fix: Lift out the pork and beans with a slotted spoon. Reduce the sauce in a pan over high heat for 10 minutes. Return everything and stir.

rows.symptom: The butter beans have fallen apart
rows.cause: Butter beans are soft and can dissolve after 8 hours of cooking.
rows.fix: Stir them through the sauce; they will thicken it. Next time, add the butter beans in the last 2 hours to keep their shape.

rows.symptom: The paprika flavour is very faint
rows.cause: The two teaspoons of smoked paprika spread through a large stew can be subtle.
rows.fix: Stir in another teaspoon of smoked paprika at the end. A pinch of cayenne will add heat as well.

content.text: Pork and bean stews are a cornerstone of Spanish and Portuguese home cooking. The fabada asturiana of northern Spain uses white beans and cured pork in a similar way, and the Portuguese cozido adds similar ingredients to a one-pot braise. This version strips the recipe back to its essentials: pork, beans, smoked paprika, and time.
